prompt: A ride-hailing company's share in one city fell from 60% to 45% in six months after a rival cut prices 20%. The company's own prices were unchanged. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Riders who care about price are likely switching to the cheaper rival.
options.feedback: Right. Share fell right after the rival cut prices 20%. I'd compare share loss by trip type and time of day, where price matters most.

options.text: The company has probably raised prices and lost riders.
options.feedback: The company's own prices were unchanged.

options.text: Price is the only factor, so the company needs to match the cut now.
options.feedback: This states one cause as certain and jumps to a price war before any data.

options.text: Riders are likely leaving because of long wait times.
options.feedback: Possible, but nothing points to it. The share loss lines up with the rival's 20% cut.

explanation: The data shows share falling from 60% to 45% right after a rival cut prices 20%, with the company's prices unchanged. Likely cause: price-sensitive riders are switching. To test it, compare share loss by trip type and time of day. If share fell as much where price matters least, look at wait times or driver supply.
